title: One custom skill 'PR Creator with Docs': before opening a PR it diffs the branch and updates the per-feature CLAUDE.md files so documentation stays the source of truth (claims 50 hrs/month saved)

tools.name: PR Creator with Docs (custom skill)
tools.detail: his own Claude Code skill; analyses all branch changes, finds the relevant CLAUDE.md/context files and updates them before creating the PR

tools.name: Per-feature CLAUDE.md files
tools.detail: one CLAUDE.md per major feature, each the source of truth for that feature; many CLAUDE.md files visible in file tree

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.detail: terminal running /agents and the Claude Code side panel

claims: This single skill saves him 'over 50 hours every single month'
He only uses one custom skill in his whole AI coding workflow
Each major feature has its own CLAUDE.md as source of truth; the skill finds exactly which one to update
how_to_steps: Keep one CLAUDE.md per major feature folder, each describing that feature
Make a skill that, when asked to create a PR, reads the full diff of the branch
Have it locate the CLAUDE.md / context files touched by the diff and rewrite them to match the new code
Then let it write and open the PR

relevance.why: Docs drift is the #1 reason CLAUDE.md goes stale for a solo founder; a pre-PR 'update the docs from the diff' step is cheap and compounding

implement_score.why: An afternoon: write a /pr-with-docs skill (git diff main..HEAD, find nearest CLAUDE.md per changed dir, update, then gh pr create). Pairs with Anthropic's 'keep CLAUDE.md thin' guidance if the per-feature docs are referenced rather than auto-loaded

verify: 50 hrs/month is self-reported marketing; the mechanism is sound regardless
Does nesting many CLAUDE.md files blow up context (Claude Code auto-loads CLAUDE.md in subdirectories it touches)?
Skill itself not shared; must be written from scratch

gap.what: Technique: a pre-PR skill that updates per-feature CLAUDE.md files from the branch diff. Liked set has /ship-style commands (Addy Osmani) and CLAUDE.md-thin advice but not an explicit docs-sync-from-diff step
